references.citation: de Sousa Santos, B. (2014). Epistemologies of the South: Justice against epistemicide. Routledge.
references.project_function: Core theoretical foundation for Tier 1 deconstructive absence coding and Tier 4 reconstructive ecology mapping.

references.citation: de Sousa Santos, B. (2007). Beyond abyssal thinking: From global lines to ecologies of knowledges. Review (Fernand Braudel Center), 30(1), 45-89.
references.project_function: Defines the 'abyssal line' that divides visible/sanctioned knowledge from invisible/disqualified knowledge.

references.citation: Grosfoguel, R. (2013). The structure of knowledge in Westernized universities: Epistemic racism/sexism and the four genocides/epistemicides of the long 16th century. Human Architecture: Journal of the Sociology of Self-Knowledge, 11(1), 73-90.
key_concepts: Four Genocides/Epistemicides of the Long 16th Century
references.project_function: Historical bias-lens cross-referencing (Tier 3 coding) that grounds Santos's abstract monocultures in documented historical violence.

references.citation: Grosfoguel, R. (2007). The epistemic decolonial turn: Beyond political-economy paradigms. Cultural Studies, 21(2-3), 211-223.
references.project_function: Establishes that location of enunciation (where one speaks from) shapes the validity claims of research.

references.citation: Castro-Gomez, S. (2010). La hybris del punto zero: Ciencia, raza e ilustracion en la Nueva Granada (1750-1816). Editorial Pontificia Universidad Javeriana.

references.citation: Quijano, A. (2000). Coloniality of power, Eurocentrism, and Latin America. Nepantla: Views from South, 1(3), 533-580.
references.project_function: Informs the Monoculture of Naturalized Classification (MONO_CLASS).

references.project_function: Analyzes how rigid insistence on standard methods functions as a technology of ontological control.

references.citation: Smith, L. T. (2012). Decolonizing methodologies: Research and Indigenous peoples (2nd ed.). Zed Books.
references.project_function: Foundational text for critiquing Western academic research as an instrument of empire.
